hypotheses.observation: policy_verdict is NO_POLICY at both the run level and inside capacity_summary, while all three stage verdicts are PASS (verified_bound_load 5, 10, 20). Each of the three window_policy_summary entries pairs business_verdict PASS with resource_verdict NO_POLICY. The only resource rules in the evidence are three resource_policy_check entries for series_id generator-cpu-throttle-ratio with effect "diagnostic", operator gt, threshold 0.2, and status PASS.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The resource side of the run may have no binding (non-diagnostic) resource policy or no declared required capacity, so it evaluates to NO_POLICY and the overall verdict can be neither PASS nor FAIL. A diagnostic generator guard is diagnostic by contract and does not supply that binding rule. This reads as a configuration state rather than a measured failure of the system under test.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the policy configuration used for this run: list resource rules bound to the SUT entities (checkoutservice, frontend, paymentservice) and their effect values, and check whether any required capacity is declared. If either is absent, add it and rerun. Expect the verdict to remain NO_POLICY until a policy or required capacity exists — a rerun by itself, or another healthy business window, does not change NO_POLICY.

caveats: The deterministic verdict is preserved exactly and is not altered by this advice: run_validity = VALID, policy_verdict = NO_POLICY, analysis_coverage = COMPLETE with empty reasons, findings = []. NO_POLICY is distinct from both PASS and FAIL; a missing policy or missing required capacity yields NO_POLICY, and neither a rerun nor a healthy business window converts it to PASS.

capacity_knee is null with knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED. This is a fixed limitation of the product, not a defect of this run and not a step an operator can take; no capacity bound here depends on a knee, and no knee detector should be implemented or enabled on the basis of this analysis.

The capacity result is bound_type LOWER_BOUND with lower_inclusive 20, upper_exclusive null, load_axis "users", unit "count". It states that 20 users was verified across stages with a verified product outcome; it does not establish a maximum, a limit, or any behavior above 20 users.

All three stage verdicts (r1-users5, r1-users10, r1-users20) are PASS with verified_bound_load 5, 10 and 20, 30 of 30 complete bins, achieved_statistic p05_10s and target_tolerance_ratio 0.1. Each corresponding window_policy_summary pairs business_verdict PASS with resource_verdict NO_POLICY, so PASS at stage level does not imply a resource-policy pass.

The three resource_policy_check entries on generator-cpu-throttle-ratio have effect "diagnostic" and status PASS against operator gt and threshold 0.2. A generator guard is diagnostic by contract: it never creates an upper bound, its effect must not be changed to binding/SLA/enforcing, and PASS here means the guard did not trip — not that generator headroom was proven.

Counts are comparable only within the same scope and window. Overall sample_count 132623 and every throughput_rps denominator 1101102 span the whole run, while the policy-check denominators 30399, 36581 and 45668 span 300000 ms windows each; the three windows cover only part of the run (with 70000 ms gaps between them), so these figures are different quantities and are not inconsistent with one another.

clock_alignment is "not_verified_by_core". No lead/lag ordering, no temporal causal claim, and no alignment of resource movements with specific JMeter samples is supported by this evidence; clock verification must come first.

Epoch fields are timestamps in milliseconds, not durations. Durations quoted above are derived differences between explicitly paired from/to fields (for example run_from_epoch_ms and run_to_epoch_ms); no raw epoch value is treated as an elapsed time.

An empty findings array, COMPLETE coverage, 30 of 30 observed cells, missing_cells 0, longest_gap_cells 0, flat jmeter_active_threads series and zero errors do not prove stability, spare capacity, low load, or the absence of a problem. They describe the analysis performed, not the health of the system under test.

Resource statistics are interval_mean aggregates over 30 cells per window; sub-interval peaks can be smoothed by that aggregation, and the reported per-window slope_per_second values are window-local and change sign between windows for paymentservice.

No CPU or memory limits, requests, or required-capacity values appear for any entity, so absolute values (for example frontend ≈0.187 cores, paymentservice ≈33.2 MB) cannot be expressed as utilization or judged against a capacity denominator.

Resource summaries exist only for the three 300000 ms evaluation windows. The snapshot extent (1790634100000→1790635330000) is wider than the run extent and the evaluation extent (1790634210000→1790635250000) is narrower, so time outside those windows — including ramp periods and inter-window gaps — is not characterized by these summaries.

No latency, throughput, or per-transaction policy thresholds are present; all latency figures (overall p50 94 ms, p95 202 ms, p99 298 ms, max 2406 ms, and the per-transaction values) are descriptive and were not evaluated against any limit.
This is a single run over one JTL CSV with no repeat executions, so run-to-run variability, warm-up effects and reproducibility of the 5/10/20-user results are unknown.

This advice interprets one immutable analysis artifact only. It cannot re-derive, re-measure, or verify the underlying JTL or resource data, and it introduces no new measurements, confidence figures, or causal claims; every hypothesis above is a candidate explanation with a bounded check, not a proven cause.
